key_insight: Long-tail fine-tune fleets pin at least one warm replica per model; pooling them onto shared GPUs with fast weight loading frees real pinned HBM for multi-model hosts.
killer_doubt: Already shipping in research and production. 'Under 1 s' cold start holds only to ~13B: 70 GB FP8 over PCIe5 x16 (~55 GB/s) takes ~1.3 s before NVMe limits.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. For sizing only: replay a public multi-model trace (Azure LLM, BurstGPT) through ServerlessLLM-style pooling and report HBM GB-hours per model at a fixed p99 TTFT.
prior_art: ServerlessLLM (OSDI'24), AlpaServe, S-LoRA/Punica multi-adapter serving, Alibaba Aegaeon GPU pooling (SOSP'25), serverless LLM hosts (Together, Fireworks).

key_insight: Fixed rate makes compressed memory addressable by arithmetic (no metadata, no fragmentation), so a CXL Type-3 'lossy fp64' NUMA node gives unmodified HPC binaries a guaranteed 2-4x.
killer_doubt: A 64 B writeback re-quantizes a whole 4^3 block (56 untouched values); drift over 1e4 timesteps at 16 bit/value may break solver bounds. HPC is ~5% of server DRAM.
decisive_experiment: userfaultfd page emulator running LULESH, an AMReX hydro code and HPCG for 1e4 steps at ZFP rates 8-32 with an RMW buffer, measuring drift versus FP64; then an Agilex CXL FPGA prototype. ~$250k.
prior_art: AVR (ICPP'19) and MemSZ lossy LLC/memory compression (Chalmers); zfp compressed arrays (LLNL); lossy-controller patent US 11347650. No inline ZFP NUMA device found.

key_insight: Duplicate of I-09037. Fold in as its host-side variant: a codec at L2 also cuts DRAM and fabric bandwidth up to ~4x for STREAM-bound stencils, which CXL cannot.
killer_doubt: Needs a CPU vendor to change the uncore, and a 4^3 block spans 16 half-lines across 4 planes, so caches need array strides. AVR/MemSZ already did LLC-side lossy.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-09037. Add one gem5 or zfp-cached-array arm at an L2-sized cache to measure bandwidth saved over the controller/CXL placement on the same three codes.
prior_art: AVR (ICPP'19) and MemSZ put lossy codecs at the LLC; zfp cached compressed arrays; FPGA ZFP codecs (DE-ZFP, ZFP-V).

key_insight: Frozen weights need no capacitor, refresh or EUV, and a via mask on a mature U.S. logic node is a real capital and sourcing lever for small, long-lived models.
killer_doubt: 28 nm via-ROM reaches ~0.05-0.13 Gb/mm2, so 70 GB FP8 needs ~4,300-11,000 mm2 (~$3-8/GB), scrapped when the model retires. HBF gives 8-16x HBM capacity at similar cost.
decisive_experiment: Desk study only: price a 28/22 nm ROM compiler macro (1-2 bit/cell) for 8B and 70B models against HBF, LPDDR and HBM in $/GB-year at 6, 12 and 24-month model lifetimes.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 hardwired Llama 8B in mask-ROM on N6 (AMD acquiring, 2026); YOLoC ROM-CiM; SanDisk/SK hynix HBF for read-only weights.

key_insight: Same mechanism as I-01226; multi-bit, stacked via-ROM chiplets fix some density, and moving weights off DRAM leaves HBM for KV cache.
killer_doubt: ROM at ~$3-8/GB is disposable after a 6-12-month model life; HBM at ~$20/GB is reused 5 years (~$4/GB-year), so ROM loses below ~2-year lifetimes. HBF is ~10x cheaper still.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-01226's desk study. Add a stacked arm (2 bit/cell, 8 dies, hybrid bond) comparing GB per package footprint and $/GB-year against HBF and HBM3E.
prior_art: Taalas/AMD hardwired-weight silicon; YOLoC ROM-CiM (2022); High Bandwidth Flash (SanDisk/SK hynix, OCP spec Aug 2026).

key_insight: Outside hyperscalers, nobody publishes what DRAM holds by workload. An on-host-aggregated atlas calibrates every compression, dedup and tiering idea here, and wedges into reclaim tooling at 4x prices.
killer_doubt: It saves nothing itself. It needs >=1,000 non-hyperscale hosts in >=10 workload classes, page hashes allow confirmation attacks, and hyperscaler data may already bound reclaimable memory at 20-50%.
decisive_experiment: eBPF/DAMON agent emitting only on-host zero/dup/entropy/coldness histograms, run 90 days on 3-5 partner fleets (university HPC, mid-size SaaS, AI inference). ~$250k. Advance if any class differs >1.5x from hyperscaler figures.
prior_art: Meta TMO, Google far memory/zswap, Microsoft Pond; Meta reports 10-20% zero pages among swapped pages (via search snippet). No public cross-fleet content atlas found.

key_insight: Counting avoided DRAM as domestic 'negabyte' supply is the right accounting frame, and procurement disclosure of bytes per transaction is executable without Congress.
killer_doubt: The 4x price spike already pays ~$4/GB-year for efficiency; a plausible $0.5-1/GB-year credit adds <25%. Counterfactual baselines invite gaming, and Jevons rebound eats savings.
decisive_experiment: Model a $0.5-1/GB-year credit against the price signal on public capex data, then pilot only the disclosure half with one agency (GSA) software buy, using the I-07673 telemetry as audit.
prior_art: Energy Star and utility demand-response baselines (gaming record), CHIPS Act credits; no memory-avoidance credit found.

key_insight: Routing easy queries to small models cuts giant-model replicas and their HBM roughly by the share of traffic that stays small.
killer_doubt: Already shipping. Escalated queries pay for both models, and 10-20% verifier misroutes erode the claimed ~3x HBM cut toward ~2x.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. For sizing: measure routed share and HBM-hours on RouteLLM benchmarks at iso-quality.
prior_art: FrugalGPT (2023), RouteLLM (2024), Hybrid LLM; production routers such as OpenAI's GPT-5 fast/thinking router.

key_insight: Textures dominate game and VR memory, and neural texture compression decoded at sample time cuts VRAM 4-8x versus BCn.
killer_doubt: VRAM is saved only when decoding at sample time; consoles, mobile and VR without matrix cores transcode to BCn on load, saving disk, not DRAM. NVIDIA already ships the SDK.
decisive_experiment: None for novelty. For sizing: measure frame-time cost and VRAM cut of decode-at-sample NTC on three GPU tiers in one Unreal scene.
prior_art: NVIDIA RTX Neural Texture Compression SDK and SIGGRAPH'23 random-access neural textures; AMD neural texture block compression; DirectX cooperative vectors.

key_insight: Decode leaves ~90% of tensor-core FLOPs idle, so online fitting of a compact learned KV for old tokens is nearly free compute. Fitted latent tokens beat a position-indexed field.
killer_doubt: Post-RoPE K/V carry token content, not smooth position signals; 20-50x needs ~0.3-0.8 bit/element versus KIVI 2-bit (8x), and querying the field costs T MLP evaluations per step.
decisive_experiment: Fit SIREN fields and online Cartridges-style latent KV per layer/head to Llama-3-8B KV at 32k tokens (exact recent window plus outliers); compare with KIVI and low-rank at equal bits on RULER. ~$30k GPU.
prior_art: Cartridges (Stanford 2025, ~38x via offline self-study), KIVI, SnapKV/H2O eviction, Palu low-rank, DeepSeek MLA, Activation Beacon.

key_insight: In batch inference the weight pass is a sequential, read-only scan, so its medium need not be DRAM. That part is right.
killer_doubt: Bandwidth is the cost: ~9 Tb/s at ~0.5 um voxels needs ~10,000 heads each tracking <100 nm; 70 GB of NAND costs ~$5, one HBF stack gives 1.6 TB/s.
decisive_experiment: Paper link budget: tracking tolerance, optical SNR and pJ/bit for a 100-head array versus ~100 Gen5 SSDs or one HBF stack at 1.25 TB/s. Build nothing unless heads cost less than SSDs.
prior_art: Microsoft Project Silica (archival glass, slow read); multi-beam optical pickups; SSD/HBF weight streaming (Apple 'LLM in a flash', HBF).

key_insight: The per-step weight stream is identical across replicas, so multicast could free weight HBM for KV in SRAM-only accelerators or small-TP replica fleets without a scale-up fabric.
killer_doubt: Wide TP/EP already keeps one copy per scale-up domain, each GPU reading W/N at ~8 TB/s; broadcast makes every GPU ingest all W (1.4 TB/s, 70B at 20 tok/s).
decisive_experiment: On an 8xH100 node, stream layer shards each decode step with NVLink SHARP multicast and compare tok/s per HBM GB against TP=8 at equal p99 latency. ~$20k of cloud time.
prior_art: Cerebras weight streaming (MemoryX/SwarmX broadcast tree), DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference, NVLink SHARP multicast, DeepSeek wide-EP decode across ~144 GPUs.
